description: Issue #923 (P0), the security-critical enforcement point: FrameworkServiceExtension.AddWtmAuthentication's Development-only ephemeral-key carve-out must be gated on a genuine environment determination -- IsDevelopmentEnvironment(services), which checks a registered IWebHostEnvironment first and falls back to ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT/DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT, defaulting to non-Development (fail closed) when neither is available. This mutant neutralizes that gate at its single call site: `bool eligibleForDevelopmentCarveOut = !isTooShortButNotPubliclyKnown && IsDevelopmentEnvironment(services);` becomes `... && true;` -- the environment check is deleted, so ANY unset/publicly-known weak key is now treated as Development-carve-out-eligible regardless of the actual hosting environment. Under the mutant, a Production deployment shipped with the demo's default appsettings.json (SecurityKey unset, or still 'super') no longer throws at startup -- it silently generates a random ephemeral signing key and boots. This is a narrower defect than the original P0 (it is not the public-demo-key forgery hole re-opened -- the generated key is genuinely random, not public), but it is still a real regression: it converts a loud, actionable startup failure into a silent misconfiguration that invalidates every access token on every restart, exactly the scenario docs/production-readiness.md's residual-exposure item (5) warns about ('production 被誤標 Development 會靜默取得臨時金鑰'), except here it is not a misdetected environment -- it is no detection at all. Four red tests, all through the real public entry point services.AddWtmAuthentication(config) with a mocked Production IWebHostEnvironment registered: AddWtmAuthentication_UnsetKey_ProductionLikeEnvironment_Throws, AddWtmAuthentication_DemoKeySuper_ProductionLikeEnvironment_Throws, AddWtmAuthentication_ExplicitWellKnownDefault_ProductionLikeEnvironment_Throws, AddWtmAuthentication_DemoKeySuperSecretKey345_ProductionLikeEnvironment_Throws -- each asserts Assert.ThrowsException<InvalidOperationException>, which fails under the mutant because the call now returns normally. The fail-closed test (AddWtmAuthentication_UnsetKey_NoEnvironmentInfoAtAll_FailsClosed_Throws, no IWebHostEnvironment registered and both environment variables cleared) also failed under the mutant in the same dry run but was not selected as this entry's red_tests -- it exercises the SAME `eligibleForDevelopmentCarveOut` line the mutant patches, so it is fully redundant with the four selected tests for kill-detection purposes; it remains a valid standalone regression test either way. The green positive control (AddWtmAuthentication_ShortCustomKey_ProductionLikeEnvironment_Throws) is unaffected -- a too-short-but-not-publicly-known key's `isTooShortButNotPubliclyKnown` short-circuits `eligibleForDevelopmentCarveOut` to false regardless of the (now-neutralized) environment term, so it still throws, proving the mutant's blast radius is scoped to the environment check specifically.

Expected exception type:<System.InvalidOperationException> but no exception was thrown. ', each accompanied by the Development-branch's own stderr warning line ('[WTM Security] Warning: JwtOptions.SecurityKey is unset or a publicly known value (...) -- generated a random, process-lifetime-only signing key because the Development environment was detected...'), confirming the call took the ephemeral-key path instead of throwing. AddWtmAuthentication_UnsetKey_NoEnvironmentInfoAtAll_FailsClosed_Throws also failed in the same run (5 Failed, 7 Passed out of 12 total in JwtAuthenticationStartupGateTests923) but was intentionally excluded from red_tests as redundant with the four selected (see description). Confirmed via `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant jwt923-devgen-environment-guard-neutralize`: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
